title: automat objectives catalog
$comment_ratification: Approved by the maintainer 2026-08-11 as part of the consolidated Phase 0 pre-approval ask recorded in ROADMAP.md's 'Backlog — research complete' section (the ask also covered Q23's OpRotate/rotation addition to evidence-manifest-v1, and assessment-result-v1's worksheet_summary/score sibling fields; all approved together). See schema/CHANGELOG.md's objectives-catalog/v1 entry for the shape rationale.
description: NIST's assessment-objective decomposition of a control catalog's requirements: for each requirement, the lettered determination statements an assessor evaluates (e.g. 3.1.1[a]..[f]) plus the candidate EXAMINE/INTERVIEW/TEST evidence sources NIST associates with the requirement as a whole. A NEW, STANDALONE document type — deliberately not a field added to schema/control-artifact-v1.schema.json's Control object, so that every catalog sharing that schema (cmmc-l1, 800-171r2, baseline-protection) is unaffected by this addition. An objectives catalog references a control-artifact catalog's requirement ids but does not redefine them; nothing here is authoritative requirement text, which stays in the referenced control-artifact document.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. Consumers must reject major versions they do not know.

control_catalog_id.description: The control-artifact catalog (schema/control-artifact-v1.schema.json) this objectives catalog decomposes, e.g. '800-171r2'. Every requirements[].id in this document MUST name a control id present in that catalog; a consumer resolving this document is expected to cross-reference the two.

sources.description: Provenance of the compile, same shape as control-artifact-v1's artifact.sources.

compiled_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, second precision, 'Z' suffix.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonicalized content payload: requirements[]. Excluded: schema_version and the catalog block itself (which carries this value, and whose sources entries are each vouched for by their own sha256).

catalog_id.description: Stable, lowercase, filesystem- and tag-safe identifier, matching control-artifact-v1's own artifact_id shape.

source.description: One compile input. Mirrors control-artifact-v1's $defs/source exactly, minus the 'artifact' union member: an objectives catalog is never itself a union of other objectives catalogs.

id.description: The requirement id, in the control-artifact catalog's own numbering (e.g. '3.1.1'). Must equal an id present in the control_catalog_id catalog's controls[]; that cross-reference is a Go-side obligation this schema cannot state.

assessment_methods.description: The candidate EXAMINE/INTERVIEW/TEST evidence sources NIST associates with this requirement as a whole — not per objective. NIST's own CPRT data model attaches one triple of these to the requirement, not to each lettered determination, so this schema follows that shape rather than inventing a finer one.

id.description: The objective's own id: either the bare requirement id (when the requirement decomposes into exactly one determination) or the requirement id with a bracketed lowercase letter suffix, e.g. '3.1.1[a]'. This is NIST's own CPRT identifier shape, not a value automat mints.

statement.description: The verbatim determination statement text, e.g. 'authorized users are identified.'

method_class.description: Reserved for a future per-objective method-class refinement (EXAMINE/INTERVIEW/TEST); NOT populated by this pass, because NIST's own data does not distinguish methods below the requirement level (see assessment_methods). Present in the schema so a later pass narrowing this is additive rather than restructuring.
